articles.desc: India and the Netherlands are enhancing cooperation in several sectors including shipping and green hydrogen. External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar and Dutch counterpart Tom Berendsen met to discuss strengthening bilateral relations. They reviewed ongoing engagements across areas such as trade, technology, and maritime development. Both sides emphasized the significance of the India-EU Free Trade Agreement for economic growth.

articles.title: Nvidia's Huang returns to cheers in China, but political hurdles mount on both sides
articles.desc: Jensen Huang has been reinstated as Nvidia CEO, reflecting his influence in US-China technology relations. His return comes amidst rising tensions, with the US tightening chip restrictions on China. Huang is set to face scrutiny from Congress regarding export controls shortly. Despite his popularity, the changing political landscape poses challenges for his role in bridging the two economies.

articles.title: PE/VC investments in India surge to USD 8.7 billion in October, highest monthly level in five years: EY-IVCA report
articles.desc: Private equity and venture capital investments in India surged to USD 8.7 billion in October 2026. This monthly figure is the highest recorded in the past five years, supported by eight large deals totaling USD 7.3 billion. Financial services attracted the majority of investments, amounting to USD 5.9 billion during this period. Despite the increase in investments, exit activity declined, with 21 exits valued at USD 544 million.

articles.title: Nasdaq drops over 2% as Nvidia-fueled AI rally fades, Anthropic tanks 11%: US Stock Market Live Updates
Shift in pension and insurance money to equities dampens long-term G-sec demand: RBI DG
articles.desc: The demand for long-term government securities has seen a marginal decline recently. Insurance companies and pension funds are increasingly focusing on equities instead of sovereign debt. This change has impacted the stability of the government securities market and highlighted challenges in liquidity distribution. The Reserve Bank of India emphasizes the need for a coordinated approach and broader participation from institutional investors.

articles.title: A 50 bps jumbo rate hike can lead to financial stability concerns, hurt growth: Report
articles.desc: SBI economists have lowered their rate hike expectations for the upcoming RBI policy review. They now anticipate a 0.25 per cent increase rather than the previously expected 0.50 per cent. This adjustment stems from concerns regarding financial stability and potential impacts on economic growth. The RBI's monetary policy committee is scheduled to meet from December 2 to December 4.

articles.title: India's economic activity growth hits four-year high of 9% in October: Jefferies
articles.desc: India's economic activity growth hit a four-year high of 9% year-on-year in October. The increase was largely attributed to strong industrial activity and a delayed festive season. However, rural demand indicators remained weak due to a subdued monsoon. While bank credit growth reached a nearly 12-year high, inflationary pressures intensified simultaneously. Overall, the report highlights a mixed outlook for future economic activity amidst varying consumer behaviors.

articles.title: AI boom looms over Warsh's Fed as inflation worries grow
articles.desc: Chairman Kevin Warsh of the Federal Reserve underscores the transformative impact of artificial intelligence on the economic landscape. While he conveys measured optimism about AI's benefits, he also warns of inflationary risks associated with its advancement. Recent discussions outline the challenges faced by Fed officials in navigating economic fluctuations linked to AI investments.

articles.title: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei sells shares worth USD 280.41 million following IPO
articles.desc: Dario Amodei, CEO of Anthropic, sold shares worth USD 280.41 million after the company's IPO. He reported holding 202.8 million shares and additional shares through trusts. Anthropic's initial public offering raised USD 81.34 billion and made its Nasdaq debut last week. However, the stock price experienced fluctuations, closing down from its opening price. Despite the decline, shares remained above their initial offering price of USD 83.

articles.title: RBI DG asks primary dealers to bid responsibly in G-Sec underwriting auctions
articles.desc: RBI Deputy Governor Rohit Jain has urged primary dealers to bid responsibly in government securities auctions. Jain noted instances of volatile pricing that misalign with orderly market conditions, impacting government borrowing costs. He highlighted the challenge of liquidity concentration in a few securities and called for improved market-making activities. Jain also pointed out declining demand from institutional investors for long-term sovereign debt amid uncertain interest rates.

articles.title: IIFCL IPO: Govt plans to sell part of its stake, company to issue fresh shares
articles.desc: The government aims to partially divest its shareholding in India Infrastructure Finance Company Ltd through an initial public offering. The IPO is expected to occur by the end of the current fiscal year, according to an official statement. IIFCL will issue fresh shares to raise capital alongside the government stake sale. The proceeds from the stake sale will contribute to the government's disinvestment revenue.

articles.title: Meta pauses Class C share issuance amid shareholder lawsuit
articles.desc: The social media giant agreed not to issue the shares during the pre-trial and trial proceedings in the lawsuit brought by shareholders in Delaware's Court of Chancery. The trial is scheduled to begin on April 19, 2027.

articles.title: Investors mint Rs 34.61 lakh cr in November as markets rally nearly 11%
articles.desc: In a remarkable surge this month, Indian equity markets have observed a substantial upswing, with the BSE Sensex climbing nearly 11 percent. This rally was largely propelled by foreign institutional investors, who contributed record-setting inflows exceeding Rs 1 lakh crore. Motivated by lower crude oil prices and impressive Q2 earnings, investor optimism soared, although a recent profit booking saw a minor dip of nearly 2 percent.

articles.title: Anthropic launches Claude Ship to help developers ship code faster
articles.desc: Anthropic said on Monday it has launched Claude Ship to help developers ship code faster by reviewing changes, fixing problems and deciding which ones can be added to the main code based on rules set by a team.

articles.title: India, Canada 'very close' to conclude trade pact negotiations: Official
articles.desc: Negotiators from India and Canada are engaging daily to finalize the Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement negotiations. A sixth round of discussions took place recently, focusing on key areas such as trade and investment. Both countries aim to increase bilateral trade to USD 50 billion by 2030, after a decline in trade values. India is also working on a separate bilateral investment protection agreement with Canada.

articles.title: Amazon to buy Decart's AI chip optimisation tech in latest AI talent grab

articles.title: Jensen Huang's Nvidia return sparks relief for battered AI trade, but questions remain
articles.desc: Huang's reinstatement atop the semiconductor giant halted a slide in technology shares that had sent the benchmark S&P 500 into a correction, though there was also some caution that his second coming may raise new risks for the company and industry.

articles.title: India-EU free trade pact to open new opportunities for trade, investment: German state leader
articles.desc: India and the European Union concluded negotiations on a Free Trade Agreement that is set to be finalized soon. Minister-President Olaf Lies of Lower Saxony emphasized the potential benefits for both Indian and German businesses. He mentioned cooperation in areas like digitalization and artificial intelligence as key prospects for collaboration. The partnership aims to enhance skilled workforce mobility with training programs for young Indians.

articles.title: HDFC Bank, Reliance Industries among 10 stocks with highest DII holding in Q2. See full list
articles.desc: With the rise in the share of MFs and also an overall net investment of  Rs 1.69 lakh crore during the quarter, the share of Domestic Institutional Investors (DIIs) as a whole increased to an all-time high of 19.31% as on September 30, 2026, up from 19.16% as on June 30, 2026. articles.title: The LTCG debate: Why markets need tax stability and not ad-hoc fixes
articles.desc: Foreign Institutional Investor capital is leaving Indian markets, raising concerns over the unpredictability of tax policies. Investors are urging for the reconsideration of Long-Term Capital Gains tax provisions. Historical changes in LTCG have created volatility that affects long-term investors negatively. A stable tax policy framework is essential to attract and retain investment in the Indian financial market.

articles.title: Nvidia and board still face legal risks after Jensen Huang's return
articles.desc: The reported ties between Huang and a suspected spy led to his resignation as CEO and sparked investigations by the US securities regulator and FBI, congressional hearings, a review by the company's independent directors and a proposed investor class action lawsuit.

articles.title: Bitcoin fails to hold Nvidia bump with crypto headwinds in focus
articles.desc: Bitcoin's recent 1% decline has overshadowed positive developments from Nvidia, leading to a dip in investor confidence. The fallout from the Binance hack and notable ETF outflows has further complicated the situation. With the Federal Reserve's potential rate hikes looming in December, many investors are hesitant, preferring to wait for clearer recovery signals despite attractive buying opportunities at current levels, erasing much of Bitcoin's value since its October 2025 peak.

articles.title: "When elephants dance, everyone moves to give space": Uday Kotak on Huang's reinstatement
articles.desc: Industrialist Uday Kotak has described Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia's Chief Executive Officer as one of the most consequential decisions in the history of global markets, saying the move has coincided with the recovery of USD 1 trillion in Nvidia's market capitalisation and USD 4 trillion across the US market.

articles.title: South Korea’s Kospi rockets 8% as AI-linked stocks get breather after Jensen Huang’s return as Nvidia CEO. Worst over?
articles.desc: South Korean shares have bounced back sharply after previously hitting a ten-month low, with the KOSPI index climbing 7.19%. This surge was largely driven by a rebound in technology stocks, particularly following Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's return to leadership. Notable AI companies such as Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix recorded substantial gains, while foreign investments showed a positive trend with net purchases totaling 497.3 billion won.

articles.title: Questions linger after Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia
articles.desc: Jensen Huang's surprise return to Nvidia on Monday appeared to stabilize the US chip giant, along with the broader stock market and AI ecosystem, but questions linger about the longterm impact of his scandal. - Will Huang's return stabilize the market?

articles.title: Japanese bond yields fall as lower oil prices ease inflation concerns
articles.desc: Japanese government bond yields declined due to falling oil prices that eased inflation concerns. The 10-year JGB yield reached a two-week low of 2.715%. Meanwhile, Japan's benchmark Nikkei 225 index experienced a brief surge of 5% following Nvidia's leadership announcement. Shorter-dated US Treasury yields increased as market stability was reassured by the news. Additionally, markets anticipate a 25-basis-point Federal Reserve rate hike in December.

articles.title: Dollar climbs as renewed AI euphoria fuels Fed hike bets
articles.desc: The dollar is approaching a 20-month peak, thanks to the reinstatement of Nvidia's CEO, which has instilled confidence in the markets. Meanwhile, the euro and sterling struggle against the strong dollar, with the euro hovering near an 18-month low. The market forecasts a Fed rate hike, adjusting to anticipated shifts in monetary policy.

articles.title: Asian stocks rally as Huang's Nvidia return revives AI trade
articles.desc: Asian shares saw significant gains as Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang made a return that relieved market fears. The MSCI Asia-Pacific index rose by 4.6%, while Japan's Nikkei gained 4.5% after a local holiday. This movement followed a 31.5% surge in Nvidia shares, revealing optimism in the beleaguered AI sector. United States Treasury yields climbed alongside the dollar, signaling increased confidence in Fed tightening measures.

articles.title: Nvidia’s board was no match for Trump or Jensen Huang’s backers
articles.desc: Trump even dialed into an Nvidia board meeting to argue for Huang’s return, according to Semafor, citing people familiar with the matter whom it didn’t identify. Asked if Huang would have been put back in place without his intervention, Trump told CNBC, “I believe my intervention was very important.”

articles.title: US blacklists Megaspeed chip firm linked to Nvidia scandal
articles.desc: The addition of the company follows revelations that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had a relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman and Megaspeed's controlling shareholder who is reportedly alleged to be a spy for Beijing.

articles.title: Jensen Huang's comeback to Nvidia underscores his outsized grip on AI
articles.desc: Clad in his trademark black leather jacket, hand on heart, the 63-year-old CEO smiled at cheering employees who packed an atrium and crowded the balconies above.

articles.title: India’s rupee has become an accidental carry star
articles.desc: The Reserve Bank of India has made moves that temporarily attract carry traders to the rupee. Recent factors include decreasing oil prices and a shift in foreign investment from artificial intelligence stocks to Indian markets. However, these RBI incentives may not last, leaving uncertainty for traders. India's interest rate advantage has significantly diminished since 2011, raising concerns. Policymakers face challenges in ensuring sustained interest in the rupee amid historical depreciation.

articles.title: Wall Street soars on Huang's return to Nvidia, Treasury yields rise
articles.desc: US stocks rebounded sharply on Monday after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive following pressure from President Donald Trump, reversing part of last week’s tech-led market rout. Nvidia jumped 31%, helping the Nasdaq 100 rise 6.5% and the S&P 500 4.7%, while Treasury yields and the dollar also climbed as investors reassessed both AI-sector sentiment and the Federal Reserve outlook.
